title: `round(d)`: `op(x · 10ᵈ) / 10ᵈ`, no negative `d`
verdict: matches the reference on the edge cases; `d < 0` refused
description: `round(d)` multiplies by `10ᵈ`, rounds (half to even unless `mode` says otherwise) and divides back; from `d = 300` it splits the multiplier into powers of 2 and 5, from `d = 326` it returns the input, and a non-finite intermediate returns the input. The two roundings make ties of the decimal text round either way: `round(2.675, 2)` is 2.68 though the double is below 2.675, and `round(0.285, 2)` is 0.28.
A negative `d` is refused by the Python API (`OverflowError`, `decimals` is a `u32`).

The `round` docs say the `half_` modes round to the nearest rounded value, which `round(2.675, 2) = 2.68` contradicts: PL-9. The docs are silent on a negative `decimals` and on `d ≥ 326` returning the input: a docs gap.
No upstream test pins this; it may change between versions.
reference: `round` to `d` digits (#335), `TIE_AWAY_FROM_ZERO`, with negative digits. On the probe's edge cases at `d` = 1, 2, 16, 308, 309, 400 Polars and the reference agree.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.

notes: Streaming gives what in memory gives on every probe and observation cited here.

`python -m sverify_dev.probe_polars --diff --write` runs each probe one row at a time and on a 6000-row column with `collect(engine='in-memory')` and `collect(engine='streaming')`, and each observation twice: its `df(...)` frame's `select`, `with_columns`, `filter`, `sort`, `unique`, `join` and `group_by` go through the streaming engine the second time (`StreamingFrame`); the `s-` observations collect a lazy query on each engine themselves. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), macOS arm64.

evidence.note: 'half_' strategies 'round all values to the nearest rounded value, only using the strategy to break ties when a value falls exactly between two rounded values' (SRC py-polars/src/polars/expr/expr.py L2001-L2025). Contradicted: round(2.675, 2) is 2.68 though the double 2.67499999999999982… is nearer 2.67. Drafted as a docs entry (PL-D2).

`test_round`: lazy collect(), Float32/Float64, (1835.665, 2) expected 1835.67, (1.005, 2) 1.0, (1e-20, 20) 1e-20, rel_tol 1e-5. Py-2.1.0 returns 1835.66 for the default mode and the test passes on tolerance: it does not pin the x * 10^d rounding. No test for d >= 300.

pl.LazyFrame({'x': [2.675, 1835.665, 0.285, 1.005]}).select(e=pl.col('x').round(2), a=pl.col('x').round(2, mode='half_away_from_zero')).collect(engine=...) with POLARS_IDEAL_MORSEL_SIZE=64: in-memory and streaming both e [2.68, 1835.66, 0.28, 1.0], a [2.68, 1835.67, 0.28, 1.0]; Python round gives [2.67, 1835.66, 0.28, 1.0] (Polars 2.1.0, macOS arm64).
